fixes.explanation: The text says the opposite, friend. "The locusts were not given power to kill them, but only to torment them for five months…" The power they get is to torment, and it has a limit. So the statement flips what the verse says.

That's it, friend. John, who is seeing this vision, says the star "…was given the key to the pit of the Abyss." Notice the star is handed the key, like a manager handing over the shop keys at closing time.

A sharp sickle does turn up in Revelation, but later on (Revelation 14:14), and not in this scene. Here the star is given the key to the pit of the Abyss. A sickle is for cutting and a key is for opening, and this verse hands out a key.

Correct, the statement is false. The locusts "…were told not to harm the grass of the earth or any plant or tree…" They're told to harm only those who did not have the seal of God on their foreheads. Real locusts would be eating the whole yard by now, but these ones get told something very different.

Yes. The locusts are told to harm "…only those who did not have the seal of God on their foreheads." The seal is the whole dividing line in this verse. Earlier in Revelation, God's servants are sealed on their foreheads too (Revelation 7:3).
You've got it. The verse says "…the locusts looked like horses prepared for battle…" Not just horses, but horses prepared for battle. That's quite a picture to get from a bug.

Plow horses are a different picture from this verse. It says "…the locusts looked like horses prepared for battle…" The comparison is to horses prepared for battle, not horses working a field. A plow horse would have a few questions about this crowd.

That's right. John says the locusts "…had breastplates like breastplates of iron, and the sound of their wings was like the roar of many horses and chariots rushing into battle." So there's armor like iron, and a sound like horses and chariots rushing into battle. I think that's a lot to take in at once.

The prince of Persia is mentioned in a different book, Daniel (Daniel 10:13), and not here. In this verse the locusts "…were ruled by a king, the angel of the Abyss." Different book, friend, and a good guess.
That's what the text says. The four angels "…were released to kill a third of mankind." This is a heavy verse, and I think it hurts to read.

Yes. John says, "…the number of mounted troops was two hundred million; I heard their number." He says he heard the number, not that he counted it. Two hundred million is a number I'd want to hear twice.

That's right. The verse says, "The heads of the horses were like the heads of lions…" The riders have breastplates the colors of fire, sapphire and sulfur, and the horses have heads like the heads of lions. That's a lot to take in at once.
That's right. John says the idols "…cannot see or hear or walk." These are idols of gold, silver, bronze, stone and wood. The verse says the rest of mankind still did not stop worshiping them.

There's no earthquake in this verse. John describes the idols as things that "…cannot see or hear or walk." The verse also names what they're made of, gold, silver, bronze, stone and wood, and says people did not stop worshiping them.
